title: Grateful Dead Live at Mammoth Gardens on 1970-04-24
lineage: AUD > master C-120 > reel 3.75ips > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN > WAV > SHN

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality audience tape, but the show shines with an iconic Dark Star and a stunning The Eleven.
ai_review.review: The remastered 1970 AUD captures a historic performance that many fans rate highly despite its tinny, bottom‑heavy sound. Highlights include a soaring Dark Star, a rollicking St. Stephen and one of the era’s best renditions of The Eleven, while the acoustic set sounds weak but improves as the electric material begins.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (Dark Star, The Eleven, Easy Wind) giving high show scores; recording quality is noted as rough but listenable, pulling the overall weighted rating to just above 4.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as tinny, bottom‑less and distant; limited frequency range and occasional pitch fluctuations, but Sir Mick’s cleanup reduces some issues and preserves the room ambience.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set dominates with a powerful Dark Star that segues into The Eleven, punctuated by a rollicking St. Stephen and an inspiring Easy Wind; the acoustic opening is thin but builds toward the electric climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is clear and intense – reviewers note he ‘goes OFF’ and his tone is tight, focused and driving.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is hard to hear in the early acoustic portion but improves later; no specific praise beyond that.
band_member_comments.Drums: A brief drum solo is mentioned before the jam leading into Good Lovin' (cut), highlighting Bill Kreutzmann’s contribution.
